long_biography.plain_text:
Electrical engineering gave Ming Hsieh both his commercial discipline and the focus of his largest public gifts. After transferring from South China to USC, he earned two engineering degrees before developing fingerprint-identification systems at Cogent. His support later endowed USC's electrical-engineering department and created an institute connecting engineering with cancer medicine.

Cogent's acquisition did not end Hsieh's company-building. He founded Fulgent in 2011 and now leads its genetic-testing, laboratory-services and therapeutic-development businesses as chairman and chief executive. He also remains an active USC trustee and currently serves on Fortinet's board.
